purpose: Execution of chapter 10 of the UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts (2016 edition): the scope of the chapter, the general three-year and the maximum ten-year limitation periods, the limits of their modification by the parties, a new period from an acknowledgement of the debt, suspension by judicial, arbitral and alternative dispute resolution proceedings as well as by force majeure, death and incapacity, and the effects of expiry. The types for party and contract and the organ come from the hub `unidroit.picc`. The 1980 UN Convention has no such chapter at all. The list of questions and boundaries is in analysis/questions.json and QUESTIONS.md.
limitations: THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).

THE 1980 UN CONVENTION HAS NO SUCH CHAPTER AT ALL: limitation is outside its subject matter and lives in the separate 1974 New York Convention. There is no bridge to `intl.uncitral.cisg*` here in substance, not for want of work.

THE COUNT BEGINS ON THE NEXT DAY, AND THE TEXT SAYS SO: "beginning on the day after the day…" in both parts of article 10.2. The §86 policy of the package is `start_count next_day`, so a three-year period from 10 March 2020 expires on 11 March 2023 and not on the 10th. The Principles have no calendar of business days: the periods are calendar periods.

SUSPENSION IS A FACT OF THE CASE HERE, NOT A COMPUTATION: the model answers whether the running of the period is suspended and the day before which it cannot expire, but does not recompute the remainder of the period by the days of suspension — the source gives no such rule, and inventing arithmetic for it is not permitted.

WHAT COUNTS AS ASSERTING A RIGHT IN PROCEEDINGS IS DECIDED BY THE LAW OF THE COURT OR THE ARBITRAL TRIBUNAL (articles 10.5, 10.6): this is a direct reference outwards, and it enters the model as a fact of the case.

THE THREE LIMITS ON MODIFYING THE PERIODS (article 10.3) ARE PRESENTED AS FACTS OF THE CASE: whether the general period has been shortened to less than one year, the maximum period to less than four years, or extended to more than fifteen. The model does not compute the comparisons itself, because the agreed periods arrive as data.
